examples.ko: 할머니는 외손자가 오는 날을 손꼽아 기다리세요.
examples.en: Grandmother counts the days until her grandson visits.
Our grandson has already become an elementary school student.

examples.ko: 외손자에게 용돈을 주고 싶어서 은행에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the bank because I wanted to give my grandson some pocket money.

examples.ko: 할아버지께서 외손자 이름을 직접 지어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandfather named his grandson himself.
He is a person who cherishes his daughter's son and his son's son equally.

examples.ko: 마을 어른들께 외할아버지 성함을 말하며 외손자라고 인사드렸어요.
examples.en: I greeted the village elders by saying my maternal grandfather's name and that I was his grandson.

explain: 아들 쪽 손자는 '친손자'라고 구별해요. 손녀는 '외손녀'예요. 앞에서 부를 때는 보통 이름으로 부르고, '외손자'는 남에게 소개하거나 이야기할 때 써요.

phrases.en: Grandmother loves her son's son and daughter's son equally.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아들 쪽 손자와 딸 쪽 손자를 구별해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell apart a son's son and a daughter's son.

phrases.en: My daughter's son was born last month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁜 소식을 전할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when sharing happy news.

phrases.en: These days grandmother takes care of her daughter's son.
phrases.nuance_ko: 할머니나 할아버지가 손자를 키우는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when grandparents look after a grandchild.

explain_en: A grandson on the son's side is called '친손자', to tell them apart. A granddaughter is '외손녀'. To their face people usually call them by name; '외손자' is used when introducing or talking about them.

examples.en: Our teacher's classes are always humorous.

examples.ko: 유머러스한 사람과 있으면 시간이 빨리 가요.
examples.en: Time goes by fast when I'm with a humorous person.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 인터뷰도 유머러스하게 해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That actor does his interviews humorously too, so he is popular.
The content was funny, so I laughed while reading the book.

examples.ko: 저는 유머러스하지 않아서 농담을 잘 못해요.
examples.en: I'm not humorous, so I'm bad at making jokes.
If you start a presentation humorously, the mood gets better.

explain: 사람의 말이나 글, 분위기가 웃음을 주는 좋은 느낌일 때 써요. 그냥 '웃기다'는 상황이 우스울 때도 쓰지만, '유머러스하다'는 재치 있고 센스 있다는 칭찬에 가까워요. 외래어에서 온 말이라 '유머 감각이 있다'로 바꿔 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Our team leader is a humorous person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun.

phrases.en: That movie wasn't very humorous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃음이 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something isn't funny.

phrases.example: 동생은 유머 감각이 있어서 같이 있으면 재미있어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling has a sense of humor, so it's fun to be around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 사람의 성격을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but used more often to describe a person's character.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a sense of humor

explain_en: It is used when someone's words, writing or mood is pleasantly funny. '웃기다' can describe any funny situation, while '유머러스하다' is closer to praising someone as witty. It comes from a loanword, and people also say '유머 감각이 있다' instead.

examples.en: My teacher is a benefactor of my life.

examples.ko: 어려울 때 도와준 은인을 잊지 못해요.
examples.en: I can't forget the benefactor who helped me in hard times.

examples.ko: 길에서 쓰러진 저를 구해 준 은인을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for the person who saved me when I collapsed on the street.
That person is a benefactor of our family.
I sent a small gift to my benefactor.
I cried when I met my benefactor.

explain: 큰 도움을 줘서 평생 고마워해야 하는 사람이에요. 가벼운 도움에는 '고마운 분'이라고 하고, '은인'은 정말 큰 은혜를 입었을 때 써요. 말할 때 자신을 낮추고 상대를 높이는 진지한 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 저를 구해 준 분은 생명의 은인이에요.
phrases.en: The person who saved me is my lifesaver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목숨을 구해 준 사람에게 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for someone who saved your life.

phrases.en: That person is my benefactor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 도움을 준 사람을 소개할 때 쓰는 해요체 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite sentence for introducing someone who helped you greatly.

phrases.en: I met a benefactor when times were hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 때에 큰 도움을 준 사람을 만났다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says you met someone who helped you greatly in a difficult time.

explain_en: A person who helped you so greatly that you stay grateful for life. For a small favor Koreans say 고마운 분, and 은인 is reserved for a real debt of gratitude. It is a serious word that lifts the other person up.

t90.ax: I cried when I met my benefactor.

examples.en: Both blood relatives and in-laws came to the wedding.
I often meet my relatives by marriage during the holidays.
I heard he is a distant in-law of the boss.

examples.ko: 서류에 인척 관계를 적는 칸이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a box on the form to write your in-law relationship.

examples.ko: 인척이 많아서 이름을 다 외우기 힘들어요.
examples.en: I have so many in-laws that it's hard to remember all the names.
They say the company doesn't hire relatives by marriage.

explain: '인척'은 결혼으로 가족이 된 친척이에요. 피로 이어진 친척은 '혈족'이라고 하고, 둘을 합쳐 '친척'이라고 말해요. 일상 대화보다 서류나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: On holidays, both relatives and in-laws gather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피로 이어진 가족과 결혼으로 이어진 가족을 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names blood relatives and in-laws together.

phrases.en: The two of them are related by marriage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼으로 생긴 가족 사이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a family tie created by marriage.

phrases.en: The two families became in-laws through the marriage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼으로 가족이 되는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means becoming family through marriage.

explain_en: 인척 are relatives who became family through marriage. Blood relatives are called 혈족, and together both are 친척. You see 인척 more in documents and news than in daily conversation.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 재결합 소식에 팬들이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Fans were surprised at the news of the two getting back together.

examples.ko: 그 가수들은 십 년 만에 재결합 공연을 해요.
examples.en: Those singers are doing a reunion concert after ten years.
A couple getting back together is not an easy decision.
When talk of a reunion came up, the mood turned awkward.
Many people are waiting for the band's reunion.

examples.ko: 회사를 나눈 뒤 재결합할 가능성은 낮아 보여요.
examples.en: After the company split, the chance of rejoining looks low.

explain: 헤어졌던 사람이나 집단이 다시 합치는 것이에요. 뉴스에서는 해체했던 그룹의 활동 재개, 헤어졌던 연인·부부가 다시 만나는 경우에 써요. 연인이 다시 만나는 것은 구어로 '다시 사귀다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I heard the news that the two actors got back together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 보이는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation in news and articles.

phrases.en: The group announced their reunion today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그룹이나 회사가 다시 합친다고 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a group or company announces they are getting back together.

phrases.en: My older sister is dating her ex-boyfriend again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연인이 다시 만나는 것을 말할 때 쓰는 구어 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spoken expression for a couple getting back together.

explain_en: It is people or groups who had split coming together again. In the news it covers a disbanded group resuming activity or an ex-couple reuniting. In casual speech, a couple getting back together is 다시 사귀다.

t90.ax: Many people are waiting for the band's reunion.

examples.ko: 젖먹이를 안고 병원에 가는 엄마가 보였어요.
examples.en: I saw a mother carrying a nursing baby to the hospital.

examples.ko: 우리 집에는 젖먹이가 있어서 밤에 자주 깨요.
examples.en: We have a nursing baby at home, so I wake up often at night.

examples.ko: 젖먹이 때는 하루에도 몇 번씩 먹여야 해요.
examples.en: When they are nursing babies, you have to feed them several times a day.
Please dress the nursing baby in warm clothes.

examples.ko: 그 젖먹이도 이제 웃을 줄 알아요.
examples.en: That nursing baby can smile now too.

examples.ko: 동생이 젖먹이처럼 자꾸 안아 달라고 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling keeps asking to be held like a little baby.

explain: 아직 젖이나 분유를 먹는 시기의 아기를 말해요. 일상에서는 그냥 '아기'라고 말해도 되고, '젖먹이'는 이야기나 글에서 아주 어린 아기를 강조할 때 어울려요. 태어난 지 얼마 안 된 아기는 '갓난아기'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The nursing baby fell asleep in its mother's arms.
phrases.nuance_ko: '젖먹이'가 아기를 꾸며서 아주 어린 아기라는 점을 더 분명히 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here 젖먹이 modifies 아기 and makes clear the baby is very young.

phrases.example: 젖먹이를 키우는 엄마는 밤에 잠을 잘 못 자요.
phrases.en: A mother raising a nursing baby can't sleep well at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 어린 아기를 돌보는 일을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is often used when talking about caring for a very young baby.

phrases.en: A newborn baby was born next door.
phrases.nuance_ko: '젖먹이'는 젖을 먹는 시기를, '갓난아기'는 태어난 지 얼마 안 된 때를 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 젖먹이 stresses the nursing stage, while 갓난아기 stresses having just been born.

explain_en: It refers to a baby who is still drinking milk or formula. In daily talk you can just say '아기', and '젖먹이' fits stories or writing that stress how very young the baby is. A newborn is called '갓난아기'.

examples.en: My friend's grandmother is coming this afternoon.
I have to write my grandmother's name on the form.

examples.ko: 조모와 함께 살았던 집이 아직 있어요.
examples.en: The house where I lived with my grandmother still exists.
I am going to see my grandmother this weekend.

examples.ko: 조모는 어릴 때 이야기를 자주 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother often told me stories from her childhood.
My grandmother will also attend the wedding.

explain: 평소에는 '할머니'라고 하고, 조모는 서류나 격식 있는 글에서 써요. 남의 할머니는 '조모님'이라고 높여요. 엄마 쪽 할머니는 '외조모'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I go to my grandmother's house every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소에 가장 많이 쓰는 말이에요. 조모는 서류나 글에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word used most in daily life. 조모 is for documents and formal writing.

phrases.en: Is your grandmother in good health?
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 할머니를 높여 부를 때 써요. 격식 있는 자리에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to respectfully refer to someone else's grandmother. Fits formal situations.

phrases.en: My maternal grandmother lives in Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 엄마 쪽 할머니를 격식 있게 부르는 말이에요. 평소에는 '외할머니'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal word for your mother's mother. In daily life people say 외할머니.

explain_en: In daily life people say 할머니, and 조모 appears in documents and formal writing. Someone else's grandmother is the honorific '조모님'. A mother's mother is '외조모'.

t90.ax: My grandmother will also attend the wedding.

examples.en: The whole nation cheered for the players with one heart.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 한마음이 되어 위기를 넘겼어요.
examples.en: Our team became of one mind and got through the crisis.

examples.ko: 한마음으로 노력하면 못 할 일이 없어요.
examples.en: If we work with one mind, there is nothing we can't do.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 한마음이라 말하지 않아도 잘 통해요.
examples.en: The two are of one mind, so they understand each other without words.

examples.ko: 반 친구들이 한마음으로 선생님께 선물을 준비했어요.
examples.en: The classmates prepared a gift for the teacher with one mind.

examples.ko: 한마음 한뜻으로 이 일을 꼭 해내요.
examples.en: With one heart and one will, let's get this done.

explain: 여러 사람이 같은 마음으로 뭉친다는 좋은 느낌이 있어요. '한마음으로', '한마음이 되다'처럼 자주 써요. 응원, 협력, 위기 극복 같은 상황에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: We cheered for the team with one mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모두가 같은 마음으로 행동할 때 가장 많이 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, used when everyone acts with the same heart.

phrases.en: When the game started, the audience became one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다르던 사람들이 하나로 모인다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like different people coming together as one.

phrases.en: My classmates prepared with one heart and one will.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음과 뜻이 모두 같다는 강조 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An emphatic phrase meaning both heart and purpose are the same.

explain_en: It has a warm feel of many people uniting with the same heart. It is often used as '한마음으로' or '한마음이 되다'. It suits cheering, cooperation and overcoming a crisis.

examples.en: An environmental activist came to our school.
The activist collected signatures on the street.
I interviewed a human rights activist in person.
There is time to ask that activist questions.
We picked up beach trash together with an activist.
Young activists are also increasing.

explain: '환경 활동가', '인권 활동가'처럼 앞에 분야 이름을 붙여 자주 써요. 사회 문제를 바꾸려고 움직이는 사람에게 쓰기 때문에 일반 직업 이름과는 조금 달라요.

phrases.en: A human rights activist gave a talk at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분야 이름을 앞에 붙인 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, with the field name placed in front.

phrases.en: I work as an animal protection activist.
phrases.nuance_ko: '로'를 붙여 직업이나 역할을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'ro' states a job or role.

phrases.en: I want to become an activist later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 목표를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a dream or goal.

explain_en: It usually takes a field name in front, as in '환경 활동가' and '인권 활동가'. It is for people working to change social issues, so it feels a bit different from an ordinary job title.

examples.ko: 초등학교 육 년 동안 개근을 했어요.
examples.en: I had perfect attendance for six years of elementary school.
I went to school even when sick to get the perfect attendance award.
My younger brother has perfect attendance, with no lateness or absences.

examples.ko: 일 년 내내 학교를 개근하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to attend school every day all year.
I had perfect attendance this semester too.
The teacher praised me for having perfect attendance.

explain: 학교에 하루도 빠지지 않고 나온 것을 말해요. '개근하다', '개근상'으로 자주 써요. 반대로 빠진 날은 '결석'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I was happy to get the perfect attendance award.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에 빠지지 않고 나온 학생에게 주는 상이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An award given to students who never missed school.

phrases.example: 중학교 때 삼 년 동안 개근했어요.
phrases.en: I had perfect attendance for three years in middle school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '개근'에 '하다'를 붙여 동사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds 하다 to the noun 개근 to make a verb.

phrases.en: I didn't miss a single day in order to get perfect attendance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개근은 결석이 없다는 뜻이라서 같이 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired, since 개근 means having no absences.

explain_en: It means attending school without missing a single day. It is often used as '개근하다' and '개근상' (perfect attendance award). A day you miss is called '결석'.

examples.en: I received the keys on the day I paid the balance.

examples.ko: 공사 대금을 다 치른 뒤에야 열쇠를 넘겨받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only take over the keys after paying the full construction cost.
I took over the duties from my senior and am working on them.
I decided to take over my father's shop.
Once you receive the documents, please check them right away.

examples.ko: 새 담당자가 자료를 아직 넘겨받지 못했어요.
examples.en: The new person in charge hasn't received the materials yet.

explain: 반대말은 '넘겨주다'예요. 일, 재산, 서류, 열쇠처럼 책임이나 물건을 다른 사람에게서 이어받을 때 써요. 받는 사람이 주어이고, 사람에게는 '-에게서'를 써요.

phrases.en: I took over that work from my senior.
phrases.nuance_ko: 업무를 이어받을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for taking over a task.

phrases.en: I haven't received the documents yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받지 못한 상황을 말할 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form for when you haven't received something.

phrases.en: The new person in charge took over the duties.
phrases.nuance_ko: '넘겨받다'와 비슷하지만 회사나 공식적인 자리에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '넘겨받다' but used more in workplaces and formal settings.

explain_en: The opposite is '넘겨주다' (to hand over). It is used when you take over responsibility or things like work, property, documents and keys from someone. The receiver is the subject, and the person you receive from takes '-에게서'.

t90.ax: I decided to take over my father's shop.

en: to be achieved (a target, quota or goal is reached)

examples.en: The goal is achieved.
This year's sales target was achieved.
Everyone worked hard, and the plan was accomplished.
Please write the achieved numbers in the table.
At this pace it is hard for the goal to be reached.
There are many things not achieved yet.

explain: '이루다'는 소원과 꿈에도 쓰지만, '달성되다'는 매출, 점수, 목표처럼 숫자로 잴 수 있는 것에 많이 써요. 내가 해내면 '달성하다', 결과로 이루어지면 '달성되다'예요.

phrases.en: The goal has not been achieved yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목표나 숫자를 아직 채우지 못했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the target or number has not yet been reached.

phrases.en: If the goal is achieved, we get a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면'을 붙여 조건을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with '-(으)면' to state a condition.

phrases.en: This year's goal was 100 percent achieved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자로 잴 수 있는 일에 퍼센트와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with percentages for measurable targets.

explain_en: '이루다' also fits wishes and dreams, but '달성되다' is mostly used for things you can measure, such as sales, scores and targets. When you accomplish it yourself it is '달성하다', and when it comes about as a result it is '달성되다'.

examples.en: The new movie was a huge success.
The first show was a big hit, so everyone was happy.
This school festival was a great success.

examples.ko: 작은 가게로 시작했는데 지금은 대성공 사례가 됐어요.
examples.en: It started as a small shop and has now become a big success story.
They say that song is a huge hit overseas too.

examples.ko: 대성공 소식을 듣고 팀원들이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The team members clapped when they heard the news of the big success.

explain: '대성공을 거두다', '대성공이다'처럼 써요. 반대는 '대실패'예요. 그냥 '성공'보다 훨씬 크고 기대 이상일 때 써서, 작은 일에 쓰면 과장처럼 들려요.

phrases.example: 그 가수의 첫 콘서트가 대성공을 거두었어요.
phrases.en: The singer's first concert was a huge success.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대성공'과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 대성공.

phrases.en: Today's presentation is a huge success!
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과가 아주 좋을 때 바로 말하는 해요체 서술형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A direct polite statement used when the result is great.

phrases.en: The event ended in great success.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 끝난 뒤 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the outcome once something is over.

explain_en: Common patterns are '대성공을 거두다' and '대성공이다'. The opposite is '대실패'. It is much bigger than plain '성공' and beyond expectations, so using it for small things sounds exaggerated.

examples.en: The construction wraps up this week.
The meeting wrapped up faster than I thought.
If the work wraps up well, let's have a meal together.
This year's project will be finished in December.
I'm relieved the event ended safely.
I still have homework that isn't finished.

explain: '끝나다'는 일이 단순히 끝난 거고, '마무리되다'는 끝을 잘 정리해서 완성되었다는 느낌이에요. 마지막 단계에서 쓰는 말이라 시작한 지 얼마 안 된 일에는 어울리지 않아요. 능동은 '마무리하다'로 '일을 마무리하다', '이야기를 마무리하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I'm relieved that the problem was wrapped up well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝이 좋게 정리되었다는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense that things ended in a good, tidy way.

phrases.en: The construction is in its final stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 거의 끝나 가는 시기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the period when a job is almost finished.

phrases.en: I'll wrap up today's work here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, with the person doing the finishing as the subject.

explain_en: 끝나다 just means something ended; 마무리되다 means it was wrapped up neatly and completed. It is a last-stage word and sounds odd for something just started. The active 마무리하다 is used in '일을 마무리하다' and '이야기를 마무리하다'.

dis.h: gets wrapped up or completed properly
gh: reaches its deadline; no longer accepting

p.n: 마감되다 makes it a deadline or closing time rather than the work being done.
